commodityScenario: Jul 13-14: Trump ordered the US Navy to reimpose its blockade on Iranian shipping through Hormuz and announced a 20% tribute fee on all other cargo transiting the strait (Reuters/Bloomberg). The US struck Iran for a third consecutive night, expected to continue for several more days. The IRGC struck US carrier logistics and refueling platforms at Duqm, Oman. Iran extended missile strikes to Qatar and the UAE for the first time in months, in addition to continued attacks on Jordan, Kuwait, and Oman. Brent $84.70 (Yahoo Finance Jul 14, +8.56%). Ras Laffan restart remains unlikely before late Aug 2026. Base 10%, stress 25%, tail 65%.

todaysEvents.delta: Up: Trump ordered the US Navy to reimpose its blockade on Iranian shipping through Hormuz and announced a 20% tribute fee on all other cargo transiting the strait (Reuters, Bloomberg, Jul 13-14) - a major structural escalation beyond the weekend's closure declaration.

todaysEvents.summary: US strikes Iran third consecutive night
todaysEvents.delta: Up: CENTCOM launched a third consecutive night of strikes on Iran (Bloomberg, Jul 13-14), expected to continue for several more days; IRGC struck US carrier logistics and refueling platforms at Duqm, Oman (Al Jazeera) in retaliation.

todaysEvents.summary: Iran hits Qatar, UAE first time
todaysEvents.delta: Up: Iran extended missile strikes to Qatar and the UAE for the first time in months (Al Jazeera, Jul 13), alongside continued attacks on Jordan, Kuwait, and Oman as the multi-country conflict widens further.

scenarios.label: Base
scenarios.description: A diplomatic off-ramp becomes still less likely after Trump's blockade and tribute order. Any resumption of talks would require Iran to accept both the blockade and the 20% cargo fee, which Tehran has already rejected in principle. Brent would need to settle back toward $85-95/bbl as the risk premium partially deflates. Probability cut to 10% after the blockade/tribute order and further multi-country strikes.

scenarios.label: Stress
scenarios.description: Hormuz remains under a contested US blockade with the 20% tribute fee partially enforced; sporadic Iranian strikes continue at a constrained tempo. Brent trades $100-130/bbl, JKM surges toward $25-30/MMBtu, iTraxx Asia IG breaks 150bp. ASEAN importers face severe and sustained supply chain disruption.

scenarios.label: Tail
scenarios.description: The blockade and tribute regime entrenches; Iran escalates strikes against blockade-enforcing vessels and expands attacks to further Gulf states. US strikes intensify against strategic Iranian infrastructure. Brent spikes $115-140+/bbl with sustained outages; JKM above $35/MMBtu; Asian credit markets dislocate. Probability raised to 65% after the blockade/tribute order, third consecutive night of strikes, and Iran's extension of attacks to Qatar and the UAE.

priceNarratives.Brent: Pre-shock ~$65 -> $126 wartime high intraday (Day 59, Apr 30, CNBC/CNN) -> $98.57 (Jun 3 D93 peak) -> $84.70 (Jul 14, +8.56% day, Yahoo Finance) as Trump reimposes the Hormuz blockade and demands a 20% cargo tribute; US strikes Iran a third consecutive night; Brent rallied 9.4% Jul 13 alone (Bloomberg), briefly topping $85.50 in Asia trade (Reuters). Working range $100-130 stress; $115-140+ tail.
priceNarratives.JKM LNG: Baseline $9.5 -> $23.40/MMBtu (Day 20, Reuters/Platts) -> $19.75 est. (Jul 8) -> $18.75/MMBtu (Jul 13, LNGPriceIndex.com) as Qatar extends LNG force majeure into Aug-Sept (JOGMEC) while Asian demand lull partially offsets the Hormuz risk premium. Ras Laffan full restart still unlikely before late Aug 2026.
priceNarratives.TTF Gas: Pre-shock ~$34/MWh -> €49.97/MWh (Day 33) -> €43.20/MWh est. (Jul 8) -> €50.43/MWh (Jul 13, +16.7% vs Jul 8, OilPrice.com/Yahoo Finance) as Qatar extends LNG force majeure into Aug-Sept and Hormuz transit collapses to a trickle - a new multi-month high.
